trait_value_raw: Prasophyllum lindleyanum produces seed even when emasculated (in the absence of pollination) and is likely to be apomictic
notes: Authors say 'likely' apomictic; no genetic tests were done to rule out sexually derived seed when pollinators are present (Discussion p.7). Possibly facultative apomixis (Discussion p.10).

trait_value_raw: Seed viability of P. tadgellianum is reflective of a mixed mating system, with evidence of outcross pollen limitation; hand-selfed flowers set fruit (92%) and produced seed (10% viable)
notes: 'mixed mating system consisting of both autogamy (self-pollination via a vector...) and allogamy' (Discussion p.8-9). Needs a vector: no fruit when pollinators were excluded. Under the revised breeding_system levels, the authors' 'self-pollination via a vector' is vector-assisted within-flower selfing (autogamy), not geitonogamy. The paper doesn't separate within-flower from between-flower selfing (hand-selfing treatment), so geitonogamy isn't scored. self-compatible is an INFERENCE, not a word the authors use: hand-selfed flowers set fruit (92%) and produced seed (10% viable), so the species is at least partly self-compatible. Space-delimited with the mating-system value as alternative descriptions from the same evidence.

trait_value_raw: P. frenchii also appears to have a predominantly outcrossing mating system; hand-selfed flowers set fruit (76%) and produced seed (21% viable)
notes: 'P. frenchii and P. tadgellianum are allogamous, requiring a vector to produce seed' (Discussion p.8). 'Predominantly' outcrossing, so a curator might prefer allogamy + self-compatible. self-compatible is an INFERENCE, not a word the authors use: hand-selfed flowers set fruit (76%) and produced seed (21% viable), so the species is at least partly self-compatible. Space-delimited with the mating-system value as alternative descriptions from the same evidence.
